name: Wedgewood Hotel and Spa
positioning: Family-owned boutique hotel in the heart of downtown Vancouver, across from Robson Square and the Vancouver Art Gallery, with a spa and a European country-house feel
best_for: Travelers wanting a downtown base across from Robson Square and the Vancouver Art Gallery
Couples wanting an intimate family-run hotel with a spa and couples massage suites

facts.text: The Wedgewood Hotel & Spa is in the heart of Downtown Vancouver.
The hotel's address is across from Robson Square and the Vancouver Art Gallery.
The Wedgewood is a family-owned and operated boutique hotel.
In 1984 founder Eleni Skalbania bought the former Mayfair Apartment Hotel and redesigned it, acting as her own designer.
The hotel says it opened in 1984 as the first female-owned boutique property in Canada.
The Wedgewood is a second-generation, female owned-and-operated property.
Conde Nast Traveler says even the smallest rooms have separate sitting areas and work desks.
Bacchus Restaurant & Lounge, inside the hotel, has Venetian decor and original artwork.
Afternoon tea is available daily, with teas from Vancouver purveyor Murchie's.
The hotel can arrange bike rentals and private yoga classes on request.
Conde Nast Traveler suggests renting a bike and heading for the Seawall to Stanley Park.
The Wedgewood is a Relais & Chateaux member.

highlights.text: To create the ambience of a European country house, the founder displayed art and antiques she had collected and commissioned custom-built furniture.
The Spa at the Wedgewood has a relaxation lounge, a eucalyptus steam room, private treatment rooms and couples massage suites.
Conde Nast Traveler says larger rooms can come with terraces, fireplaces and standalone bathtubs.
The 4th Baron of Wedgwood attended the hotel's opening.
Bacchus Lounge has classic cocktails and live piano performances nightly.

considerations.text: Executive Rooms have a limited laneway view.
Conde Nast Traveler describes the gym as small but serviceable, with TechnoGym equipment.
Conde Nast Traveler rates the hotel as not particularly family friendly.
